subject: Mediveil on-prem: sustained 5xx spike, throughput collapse — exec sync requested
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@mediveil.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, sre@mediveil.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate + throughput collapse on our on-prem cluster (region: us-west)

Rafael,

We started seeing a sustained spike in 5xx responses on our on-prem inference cluster around 07:45 PDT. Throughput has dropped ~60% and tail latencies are through the roof (p99 > 12s). Our SRE team attached a short Prometheus snapshot and core dump summary. Impact: production traffic for the Mediveil NLP pipeline is degraded — primary inference endpoint returning 502/504 across multiple nodes.

Initial triage (SRE):
- Frequent LLM runtime OOM and kernel-level throttling on node set B (GPUs: T4p-equivalent).
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 87% to 12% after the spike.
- Several model shards are reporting repeated RPC timeouts to the local tensor-serving daemon.

We need Redwood engineering to triage immediately. This is customer-critical; our CRO and CTO are awake on this. Can you confirm receipt and next steps?

Attachments: mediveil_prometheus_snapshot_20280620.json, core_dumps_summary.txt

Best,
Lydia
SRE Lead, Mediveil
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@mediveil.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2028 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput collapse on our on-prem cluster (region: us-west)

Lydia — received, thank you for the quick heads up and the attachments. Rafael here (Account Lead for Mediveil).

Immediate plan:
1) Scheduling a technical triage with Karthik (inference ops) and our on-call kernel team — target 09:45 PDT.
2) We will gather hot threads, request-level samples, and full tracer output. Please preserve the nodes and avoid any destructive reboots until we capture core logs (we may ask to snapshot memory).
3) Marissa will coordinate CS communications and escalate to our execs if we need temporary capacity uplift or a formal credit.

Lydia — can you confirm whether Mediveil has the option to briefly redirect a percentage of traffic to a fallback region or a host-based queue? Also confirm if you can enable detailed heap snapshots for the affected nodes; that will accelerate kernel-level diagnosis.

I will lead the customer sync and keep you updated.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput collapse on our on-prem cluster (region: us-west)

Quick note from CS side — I spoke with Mediveil ops on the phone. Current customer impact:
- ~25% of requests are falling back to sync retry path, causing downstream queueing at the app layer.
- Two critical customer SLAs are at risk for the next 2 business hours.

Customer asks right now:
- Temporary prioritization (burst capacity) if Redwood can spare reserved nodes in the region for the next 6–12 hours.
- A rollback option if the recent runtime kernel change (deployed 36 hours ago) is implicated.

We should prepare an exec-facing one-pager for their CTO highlighting the root causes we are exploring and the remediation options (capacity uplift, rollback, kv cache warm, kernel patch). I can draft the note once we have a clearer tech ask.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Lydia Park <lydia.park@mediveil.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2028 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput collapse on our on-prem cluster (region: us-west)

Triage update from infra side (Karthik):
- Root suspicion: an interaction between recent compilation kernel changes and the customer's custom tensor-sharding that increases memcpy pressure under certain sequence-length distributions. That can explain both the OOMs and the KV cache invalidation behavior.
- Data we grabbed: heap profiles, the Prometheus snapshot, and the core dump summary. I attached a short playbook for a KV cache reset and a low-risk patch we can push to reduce prefetch mem pressure (playbook_kvcache_reset.md).

Proposed immediate mitigations (non-invasive):
1) Disable the aggressive prefetch path for the affected model variant (runtime flag) — reduces mem pressure at the cost of some cold-start latency.
2) Warm KV cache by replaying recent prefixes on a spare node (we can coordinate with Mediveil SRE to replay a sampled subset).
3) If mem thrashing persists, rollback the kernel change to the previously pinned build (we need a 30–45 minute maintenance window).

If Mediveil can temporarily route 20% of traffic to a fallback queue or allow us to spin up two reserved nodes on their VLAN, we can use them as warmers and reduce p99 quickly. Please confirm options.

— Karthik Iyer
Inference Ops, Redwood Inference
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@mediveil.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Jun 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Mediveil on-prem: exec sync scheduled & ask summary

Lydia / Rajeev — thank you again for the patience while we triaged. This message confirms the exec sync for Monday 08:00 PDT (invite to follow). Attendees we propose: Mediveil CTO, Mediveil SRE lead, Rafael (Redwood Strategic Accounts), Marissa (CS), Laura (AE), Karthik (Inference Ops), and our kernel lead.

Summary of technical recommendations for the execs:
- Short-term (0–6 hours): disable aggressive prefetch flag + warm KV cache from a reserved node; enable stricter thread-level timeouts to reduce RPC cascades. (Action owner: Karthik / Mediveil SRE)
- Mid-term (6–48 hours): if behavior persists, rollback last kernel compilation change for the affected runtime (requires maintenance window). (Action owner: Kernel team / Mediveil infra)
- Customer ask: confirm whether Redwood should request temporary reserved capacity (2 nodes) for warming; also confirm the opt-in for a possible rollback.
- Commercial ask: CS to propose a one-off service credit if we miss SLA windows; recommend preparing that ahead of the exec call. (Action owner: Marissa / Rafael)

Attachments for exec packet: playbook_kvcache_reset.md, mediveil_prometheus_snapshot_20280620.json, core_dumps_summary.txt.

Please reply here with confirmation of the Monday time or propose an alternate. If you authorize the temporary reserved node uplift and the prefetch disable, Karthik can coordinate the change tonight (non-invasive).

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
